Subject: Private VPC networking follow-up / next steps

Hi Alex — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side.

Recap of your requirements (as I understood them):
- Regulated PII workloads — data must remain in your VPC / no public egress for stored data.
- Preference for private connectivity (you mentioned a bias toward PrivateLink because of firewall restrictions, but open to peering if that's easier).
- Need static IP allowlist for any outbound traffic from Redwood to partner services.
- KMS integration for customer-managed keys (encryption at rest).
- SAML SSO + SCIM for user access.
- Expected throughput: approx 200 concurrent requests peak, avg 60 req/s (we'll refine with your traffic profile).

What we can do / options:
- PrivateLink (AWS Interface Endpoint): best when your security team requires interface endpoints and strict egress controls. Requires you to create interface endpoints in your VPC; we provide the endpoint service name and cross-account permissions.
- VPC Peering: good for high-throughput use cases (no NAT traversal), requires route table updates and security group rules on both sides.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): if predictability and capacity isolation are top priority, Dedicated GPU pools are available — still supports Private VPC networking options.

Immediate next steps (proposed):
1) I attach a short network requirements PDF with the items our infra team will need. Please share your network diagram and CIDR ranges. [Attachment: network_requirements_v1.pdf]
2) Tech deep-dive: schedule a 60-min session next week with your NetOps + our SRE (Sean) to walk the diagram and confirm which connectivity pattern (PrivateLink vs peering) maps to your firewall/NAT constraints.
3) Security questions: I can share our SOC2 evidence pack and KMS integration docs in parallel — I'll loop our security PM if needed.

Can you confirm a) whether your network team prefers PrivateLink or peering as a starting point, and b) send your VPC CIDR and the preferred maintenance windows for testing?

Thanks — I'll coordinate with Sean to get the tech session on the calendar.

Best,

Hi Alex — great, thanks for the diagram. Attaching a more detailed checklist (spreadsheet) but high-level answers below.

PrivateLink vs VPC Peering — quick comparison:
- PrivateLink (recommended for strict firewall policies): you create interface endpoints in your VPC, we provide the endpoint service name and an account ID to allow the connection. This keeps traffic within AWS backbone and is compatible with strict ingress rules.
- VPC Peering (recommended for very high throughput): route-table updates required; no transitive routing. Works well if you want lower latency and large data transfers, but your firewall policy may make approvals slower.

IP allowlist / egress:
- For PrivateLink: most control-plane traffic comes over the interface endpoints; any outbound calls from our service to external third-party APIs would come from a set of static NAT IPs if you route traffic through our managed egress. We can provide a list of egress IP ranges used by the cluster once you confirm PrivateLink vs peering.
- For VPC peering: you can use your own NAT/Gateway to egress to third parties, so no Redwood-managed egress IPs are required for outbound partner calls.

Required items from FinLytics to proceed:
1) VPC CIDR(s) and preferred subnets for interface endpoints (if PrivateLink).
2) Contact info for your NetOps engineer (we'll add them to the tech session).
3) Security questionnaire items we flagged; we can fast-track SOC2 artifacts.

I'll attach the checklist spreadsheet and our Private VPC technical doc link (below). If PrivateLink is the starting point, please confirm and we'll send an endpoint service name and a temporary test endpoint in staging for validation.

Links / attachments:
- Redwood Private VPC requirements checklist [Attachment: redwood_private_vpc_requirements_checklist.xlsx]
- Private VPC doc: https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/FinLytics-PrivateVPC-Overview

- We schedule a 60-min tech deep-dive during your maintenance window (Wed 02:00-06:00 UTC).

Best,
Marissa
